one_liner: Safe-Rust zlib/deflate codec tuned for PNG data; decoder claimed on par with zlib-ng and zlib-rs, encoder still preliminary.
what_it_does: A Rust crate that reads and writes standard zlib streams (raw deflate output is also possible from the compressor; the decoder accepts zlib only, gzip/raw inflate is open issue #79). The API is Rust-native, not the zlib C API: decompress_to_vec / decompress_to_vec_bounded and a streaming Decompressor::read(input, output, output_position) that uses the caller's output buffer as the 32 KiB history window, plus compress_to_vec_with_level, compress_to_vec_rle, compress_to_vec_ultra_fast and a streaming Compressor with flush(). It is the deflate backend of the png crate; the published 0.3.x line only has the ultra-fast encoder, while main (0.4.0, unpublished) adds levels 0-7, RLE mode and flushing.
how_it_is_fast: The decoder uses a 4096-entry primary Huffman table to fit modern L1 caches, multi-symbol literal decoding (two or three literals per table lookup, the technique from Yann Collet's 'Huffman revisited part 4' post), precomputed fixed-Huffman tables and a 64-bit bit buffer refilled with one unaligned 8-byte load. The ultra-fast encoder writes a single block with one fixed Huffman tree trained on PNG images (codes of 12 bits or less) and emits only zero-run back-references, borrowing from fpnge. The 0.4 encoder uses greedy parsing with hash-table or hash-chain match finders at levels 1-3 and lazy parsing with a hybrid match finder at levels 4-7; Adler-32 comes from the SIMD simd-adler32 crate.
when_to_use: Rust programs that decode PNG or other zlib streams with many literals and want zlib-ng-class inflate speed without C dependencies or unsafe code in the codec itself.
Real-time PNG encoding where file size matters less than speed: the ultra-fast mode targets QOI-like encode speed while staying zlib-compatible.

Rust builds that track git main and want the 0.4 encoder: a third-party Zen4 run (issue #75, flate2_bench, Govdocs1 in 4 KiB chunks) measured 94.3 MB/s at level 6 vs zlib-ng 65.5 and zlib-rs 59.6 MB/s at a slightly lower ratio (1.809 vs 1.837).
Code already going through the png crate, which pulls fdeflate in for you.
when_not_to_use: C or C++ projects: there is no C API or binding; zlib-ng or libdeflate give comparable decode speed with a C interface.

Fast compression at level 1: issue #75 measured fdeflate level 1 at 91.5 MB/s and ratio 1.474 vs zlib-ng 173.7 MB/s / 1.650 and miniz_oxide 220.1 MB/s on Govdocs1 (Zen4), and the issue was closed as not planned.

Maximum ratio: levels 8 and 9 are accepted but run the same configuration as level 7 (Compressor::new maps 7.. to one LazyParser setting), and ratio stays slightly below zlib-ng at every measured level.

Decoding untrusted input where CPU time must be bounded: issue #83 (July 2026) shows chains of tiny dynamic-Huffman blocks forcing a full 4096-entry table rebuild each, about 3 s for 1,000,000 blocks with no output; it was closed as not planned and current main has no rebuild limit.
Users needing a stable released encoder: crates.io still ships 0.3.7 (2024-12-06) with only ultra-fast compression; Cargo.toml on main is publish = false.

integration.dependencies: simd-adler32 (runtime); miniz_oxide and rand only as dev-dependencies
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.88 on main (rust-version in Cargo.toml); Rust 1.67 for the published 0.3.7
integration.platforms: any Rust target; CI also runs tests on big-endian powerpc under QEMU; no architecture-specific code in the crate (SIMD only inside simd-adler32)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; Decompressor and Compressor are plain owned state objects with no shared globals, so one instance per thread

gotchas: Released 0.3.7 skips the Adler-32 update when read() returns early after flushing a queued RLE or back-reference run into a small output buffer, which can raise a false checksum error on a valid stream; main fixed it on 2026-05-27 (PR #82, test checksum_includes_queued_output) but no release carries the fix.

Issue #80 (May 2026, closed as not planned with no maintainer comment) reports a panic on malformed input when the bit count wraps; in 0.3.7 the fill_buffer fast path computes input[(63 - nbits)/8..], which panics if nbits ever exceeds 63, while main masks nbits with & 63 since PR #50 (June 2025). consume_bits still only debug_asserts against underflow on main.
Decompressor::read may write past the returned length and needs the previous 32 KiB of output kept in the same buffer; it panics if output_position is out of bounds.
#![forbid(unsafe_code)] covers this crate only; the simd-adler32 dependency uses unsafe SIMD intrinsics. The encoder always writes zlib header bytes 0x78 0x01 regardless of level.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over zlib-ng or libdeflate only inside pure-Rust stacks (especially PNG pipelines) that refuse C dependencies; from C++ use zlib-ng, which is catalogued with full lzbench numbers, or libdeflate for whole-buffer work.
verified_claims_summary: The project's own evidence is directional: README says the decoder 'rivals or exceeds' zlib-ng and zlib-rs and the encoder beats zlib-rs at levels 1-3, backed only by a corpus-bench scatter plot on the QOI corpus (discussion #68, numbers unreadable here, no CPU or compiler). The only numbers found are third-party (issue #75, flate2_bench on Zen4, Govdocs1 in 4 KiB chunks): fdeflate main was about 1.4x zlib-ng at level 6 and 1.65x at level '9' (actually level 7), but about 0.5x zlib-ng at level 1.
status_note: Actively developed (last commit 2026-05-31) and dual MIT/Apache-2.0, but the improved encoder and the checksum fix exist only on unpublished main, and two 2026 robustness reports (#80, #83) were closed without fixes.
